newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share buybacks limited to 10pct - official.
newsitem.headline: German share buybacks limited to 10pct - official.

text.p: German companies ought in future be allowed to repurchase a maximum of 10 percent of their own equity, a leading Justice Ministry official said on Monday.

Rainer Funke, state secretary of the Justice Ministry, told a conference that the government would frame a new share law on an EU directive which sets an upper limit of 10 percent for equity buybacks.
Share buybacks are currently virtually impossible in Germany because of tight legal restrictions but a new share law is expected to change that, probably in 1998.
Funke also said there was no consensus in Bonn to limit the level of corporate investments banks are entitled to hold and so no legal measures were planned on this issue.
German banks are frequently criticised for having too close links with their corporate customers via their vast network of industry shareholdings.
There were also no plans to reduce the number of supervisory board positions a German management board member was entitled to hold from the current ten, he added.
However Funke said the government planned to introduce measures to make it easier for shareholders to voice protests over the actions of supervisory board and management board members.
